parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: State what is meant by an ideal gas.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Use one of the basic assumptions of the kinetic theory to explain what can be deduced about the potential energy associated with the random motion of molecules in an ideal gas.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead:
A sample of 0.26 m³ of an ideal gas is at pressure 2.0 × 10⁵ Pa and temperature 290 K.

Determine:
parts.text: the number *N* of molecules of the gas

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: the average translational kinetic energy *E*ₖ of one molecule of the gas

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: the internal energy of the gas. Explain your reasoning.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
The volume *V* of the gas in (b) is now varied, keeping its pressure constant.

On Fig. 3.1, sketch the variation with *V* of the internal energy *U* of the gas.

[[fig:f1]]

figures.caption: Fig. 3.1
figures.alt: Blank graph axes with internal energy U on the vertical axis and volume V on the horizontal axis, both marked zero at the origin.
